Project P20890 (Angola) — Fire & Gas Control Panel (FGCP-7404-001) Pseudocode

Complete structured pseudocode translation of the GE Fanuc VersaMax PLC program (LAD/*.pdf & var.xml) and its Rockwell RSLogix 5000 v17 conversion (P20890_Angola_RSLogix5000_V17.L5X). Hover over any tag to inspect its PLC address, data type, and engineering description; click any tag to highlight all occurrences across the program.

1. Scan Cycle Pipeline (_MAIN)

IF #FST_SCN (%S00001) → CALL Init()
ELSE → CALL Input() → CALL Logic() → CALL Output()

2. Input & Voting Pipeline (Input)

DI_1 (13 DIs) → AI_1..3 (22 AIs via CalcVa1..3 & Ai_AL_1..3) → Vote_1 (Gas Lo/Hi, 56 Inhibits, 81 Faults)

3. Core Logic & Warmup (Logic)

120s Startup Stabilization Timer (T00002) with automatic 2s pre-enable reset → CE_LOG (ESD & Deluge Pump A/B) → Sound (38 Rising-Edge One-Shots)

4. Fail-Safe Outputs (Output)

Shutdow (De-energize-to-trip %Q01,03,04,08) → Protect & FLT_1 (Deluge %Q05..07 + 70s Line Watchdog) → Indicat & Loc_Al
1. Executive & Initialization

⚙ _MAIN / MainRoutine LAD/_MAIN.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 2 L5X Rungs: 4 Called By: PLC OS Cyclic Scan Calls: Init (First Scan), Input, Logic, Output (Normal Scan)

Top-level cyclic executive routine. Runs Init once on the very first PLC scan (#FST_SCN / %S00001), and executes the deterministic 3-stage pipeline (Input -> Logic -> Output) on every subsequent scan.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (_MAIN) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: _MAIN (MainRoutine) — Cyclic Scan Executive
// Source:  LAD/_MAIN.pdf (2 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

IF #FST_SCN (%S00001) THEN
    // First scan after PLC enters RUN mode: initialize timers and sound latches
    CALL Init();
ELSE
    // Every subsequent PLC scan cycle:
    CALL Input();   // 1. Read & scale DI/AI channels, evaluate alarms, faults & voting
    CALL Logic();   // 2. Run 120s startup delay, system reset, Cause & Effect, and Sound
    CALL Output();  // 3. Drive physical relay outputs (%Q0001..%Q0016) & line fault checks
END_IF;
1-to-1 Rung-by-Rung Pseudocode Translation (4 Rungs)
Rung / Source Structured Pseudocode & Ladder Logic
Rung 0
_MAIN rung 3 (GE) - %S00001 (#FST_SCN) NOCON; CALL Init
First-scan call: NO #FST_SCN (%S00001, i.e. S:FS) guards CALL Init, so the Init block runs on the first scan only and resets the two internal cause-and-effect alarm flags and clears the start-up delay/timer registers there. The printed legend above the rung reads 'Call initiate'.
IF #FST_SCN%S00001 THEN
    CALL Init();
END_IF;
XIC(S:FS)JSR(Init,0);
Rung 1
_MAIN rung 5 (GE) - %S00001 (#FST_SCN) NCCON; CALL Input
NC #FST_SCN (%S00001, i.e. XIO(S:FS) = NOT first scan) guards CALL Input, so the input-handling block runs on every scan except the first. The printed legend reads 'Call Input routine'.
IF NOT #FST_SCN%S00001 THEN
    CALL Input();
END_IF;
XIO(S:FS)JSR(Input,0);
Rung 2
_MAIN rung 7 (GE) - %S00001 (#FST_SCN) NCCON; CALL Logic
NC #FST_SCN (%S00001, i.e. XIO(S:FS)) guards CALL Logic on every scan after the first. The legend calls it 'Call LogicCE (Cause & Effect) routine' but the CALL operand - and therefore the JSR target - is the GE routine Logic.
IF NOT #FST_SCN%S00001 THEN
    CALL Logic();
END_IF;
XIO(S:FS)JSR(Logic,0);
Rung 3
_MAIN rung 9 (GE) - %S00001 (#FST_SCN) NCCON; CALL Output
NC #FST_SCN (%S00001, i.e. XIO(S:FS)) guards CALL Output on every scan after the first, so the physical outputs are driven only once the first scan is over. The printed legend reads 'Call Output routine'.
IF NOT #FST_SCN%S00001 THEN
    CALL Output();
END_IF;
XIO(S:FS)JSR(Output,0);
1. Executive & Initialization

⚙ Init LAD/Init.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 2 L5X Rungs: 3 Called By: _MAIN (First Scan Only) Calls: None

First-scan initialization block. Clears the 120s startup C&E delay timer register (%R00202), zeroes all 13 pump/deluge timer blocks (Pump_Timer1..13 at %R00205..%R00243), and unlatches the PCR and Pump House audible alarm internal bits.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Init) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Init — First-Scan Initialization
// Source:  LAD/Init.pdf (2 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// Rung 1: Clear first pump timer register, C&E startup delay register, and sound latches
Pump_Timer1[0..2]      (%R00205..0207) := 0;
System_C_E_Delay[0..2] (%R00202..0204) := 0;
UNLATCH Tag_DO_15_INT       (%M00215)  := FALSE;  // PCR Panel Alarm Buzzer
UNLATCH SA_7404_001_002_INT (%M00202)  := FALSE;  // Pump House Alarm Horn/Bell

// Rung 2: Block-clear Pump_Timer2 through Pump_Timer13 (39 contiguous INT words)
// GE Instruction: ARRAY_MOVE_INT(SRC := Pump_Timer1, LEN := 39 -> DST := Pump_Timer2)
FOR reg_addr := %R00208 TO %R00243 DO
    REGISTER[reg_addr] := 0;
END_FOR;
1-to-1 Rung-by-Rung Pseudocode Translation (3 Rungs)
Rung / Source Structured Pseudocode & Ladder Logic
Rung 0
Init rung 2 (GE) - MOVE_WORD 0 -> Pump_Timer1 (%R00209), MOVE_WORD 0 -> System_C_E_Delay (%R00202); two blocks in series, count 3 each
First-scan clear of the two 3-word cause-and-effect start-up delay registers: MOVE WORD with IN=0 and count 3 clears Pump_Timer1 (%R00209-%R00211) and System_C_E_Delay (%R00202-%R00204). The two blocks are printed in series on an unconditional rung and are emitted as one MOV per printed destination, so the count 3 is recorded here rather than folded into a COP.
Pump_Timer1[0] := 0;
System_C_E_Delay[0] := 0;
[MOV(0,Pump_Timer1[0]),MOV(0,System_C_E_Delay[0])];
Rung 1
Init rung 4 (GE) - %S00007 (#ALW_ON) NOCON -> RESETCOIL Tag_DO_15_INT (%M00239), RESETCOIL SA_7404_001_002_INT (%M00226)
First-scan reset of the two internal cause-and-effect alarm latches: RESETCOIL Tag_DO_15_INT (%M00239, 'Panel alarm - Internal C_E use') and RESETCOIL SA_7404_001_002_INT (%M00226, '7404-SA-001/002 Local alarm pump house'). #ALW_ON (%S00007) is always true so the rung is unconditional, and the two reset coils are drawn as parallel output branches (vertical bus at x=674, left of both coils).
UNLATCH Tag_DO_15_INT := FALSE;
UNLATCH SA_7404_001_002_INT := FALSE;
[OTU(Tag_DO_15_INT),OTU(SA_7404_001_002_INT)];
Rung 2
Init rung 6 (GE) - %S00007 (#ALW_ON) NOCON -> MOVE_INT 0 -> Pump_Timer1[0
(%R00209), count 42] First-scan reset of the pump delay timers: MOVE INT with IN=0 and count 42 clears 42 words starting at Pump_Timer1[0] (%R00209), i.e. the whole Pump_Timer1..Pump_Timer13 WORD arrays (%R00209-%R00247) plus three spare words. It is emitted as the single MOV to the printed destination element that the conversion rule asks for, with the count 42 recorded here.
Pump_Timer1[0] := 0;
MOV(0,Pump_Timer1[0]);

GE Rungs: 1 L5X Rungs: 6 Called By: _MAIN Calls: DI_1, DI_2, AI_1, AI_2, AI_3, Vote_1

Master input dispatcher. Sequentially invokes discrete input conditioning (DI_1, DI_2), analog input scaling & alarm evaluation across the three 8-channel analog cards (AI_1, AI_2, AI_3), and system-wide alarm/inhibit/fault voting (Vote_1).

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Input) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Input — Input Processing Dispatcher
// Source:  LAD/Input.pdf (1 Rung)
// ============================================================================

CALL DI_1();    // Discrete Input Card 1 (%I0001..%I0013) conditioning & latching
CALL DI_2();    // Discrete Input Card 2 (Empty spare subroutine)
CALL AI_1();    // Analog Input Card 1 (%AI0001..%AI0008): Point Gas Detectors 001..008
CALL AI_2();    // Analog Input Card 2 (%AI0009..%AI0016): Gas 009..010, Flame 001..002, Open-Path 011R
CALL AI_3();    // Analog Input Card 3 (%AI0017..%AI0022): Pressure Switches & Foam Pushbuttons
CALL Vote_1();  // Aggregate Gas Detector Voting, All Inhibits, and All Faults

2. Input Dispatcher & Discrete Inputs

⚙ DI_1 LAD/DI_1.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 42 L5X Rungs: 26 Called By: Input Calls: None

Processes all 13 discrete inputs (%I0001..%I0013) on the 32-channel 24VDC DI module (IC200MDL650). Generates VDU status/alarm bits (<Tag>_AL) and inhibit-gated Cause & Effect bits (<Tag>_ALI := <Tag>_AL AND NOT <Tag>_INH). Low tank level switches (LS_7503_001/002) and the fail-safe NC Fuel Gas ESD pushbutton (ESDV_6401_001) are latched until System_Reset.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (DI_1) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: DI_1 — Discrete Input Conditioning (%I0001..%I0013)
// Source:  LAD/DI_1.pdf (42 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// --- Pattern A: Unlatched Status / Pushbutton Inputs ---
// Applies to:
//   %I0001 ZSH_6401_001        (ESD Valve Open Limit Switch)
//   %I0002 ZSL_6401_001        (ESD Valve Closed Limit Switch)
//   %I0003 FS_7503_001         (Stop Foam Release Pushbutton)
//   %I0006 Pump_A_PulsIn       (Deluge Pump A Line-Check Feedback)
//   %I0007 Pump_B_Start_PulsIn (Deluge Pump B Start Line-Check Feedback)
//   %I0008 SpareDI_08          (Spare Discrete Input 8)
//   %I0009 Pump_B_Inhibited    (Deluge Pump B Selector Not in Auto)
FOR EACH tag IN [ZSH_6401_001, ZSL_6401_001, FS_7503_001, Pump_A_PulsIn,
                 Pump_B_Start_PulsIn, SpareDI_08, Pump_B_Inhibited] DO
    tag_AL  := tag;                      // Direct status to HMI/VDU
    tag_ALI := tag_AL AND NOT tag_INH;   // Inhibit-gated signal to C&E logic
END_FOR;

// --- Pattern B: Latched Tank Low-Level Alarm Inputs (Normally Open -> Close on Alarm) ---
// Applies to:
//   %I0004 LS_7503_001 (AFFF Foam Tank Low Level)
//   %I0005 LS_7503_002 (Diesel Tank Low Level)
FOR EACH tag IN [LS_7503_001, LS_7503_002] DO
    tag_AL  := (tag OR tag_AL) AND NOT System_Reset (%M00700);
    tag_ALI := tag_AL AND NOT tag_INH;
END_FOR;

// --- Pattern C: Fail-Safe Normally-Closed (NC) Latched ESD Pushbutton (Rungs 28..30) ---
// %I0010 ESDV_6401_001: Healthy = 1 (24VDC present), Pressed/Wire-Break = 0
ESDV_6401_001_AL  (%M00028) := (NOT ESDV_6401_001 (%I00010) OR ESDV_6401_001_AL)
                               AND NOT System_Reset (%M00700);
ESDV_6401_001_ALI (%M00061) := ESDV_6401_001_AL AND NOT ESDV_6401_001_INH (%M00029);

// --- Pattern D: Channels with First-Up Detection (Rungs 31..42) ---
// %I0011 SpareDI_11 (Latched), %I0012 INHIBIT_FOAM_REL (Keyswitch), %I0013 INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS (Keyswitch)
SpareDI_11_AL  (%M00031) := (SpareDI_11 (%I00011) OR SpareDI_11_AL) AND NOT System_Reset;
SpareDI_11_ALI (%M00062) := SpareDI_11_AL AND NOT SpareDI_11_INH (%M00032);
SpareDI_11_FRUP(%M00033) := ((SpareDI_11_ALI AND NOT System_AnyActions) OR SpareDI_11_FRUP) AND NOT System_Reset;
IF SpareDI_11_FRUP THEN LATCH System_AnyActions (%M00701) := TRUE; END_IF;

FOR EACH keyswitch IN [INHIBIT_FOAM_REL (%I00012), INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS (%I00013)] DO
    keyswitch_AL   := keyswitch;  // Unlatched keyswitch state
    keyswitch_ALI  := keyswitch_AL AND NOT keyswitch_INH;
    keyswitch_FRUP := ((keyswitch_ALI AND NOT System_AnyActions) OR keyswitch_FRUP) AND NOT System_Reset;
    IF keyswitch_FRUP THEN LATCH System_AnyActions (%M00701) := TRUE; END_IF;
END_FOR;

⚙ CalcVa1 LAD/CalcVa1.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 2 L5X Rungs: 4 Called By: AI_1 (Ch 1..8), AI_2 (Ch 9..13, 15..16), AI_3 (Ch 17, 19..22) Calls: None

Scales a raw 0..20 mA analog input (0..32000 counts) into a 0..100 integer engineering range (%LEL or PSI), where 4 mA (6400 counts) = 0 and 0 mA (0 counts) = -25.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (CalcVa1) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: CalcVa1 — Integer Scaling for 0..100 %LEL / 0..100 PSI
// Source:  LAD/CalcVa1.pdf (2 Rungs)
// Formula: EngVal = (((RawCounts / 32) * 125) / 1000) - 25
//   * 0 mA  (    0 counts) -> -25
//   * 4 mA  ( 6400 counts) ->   0 (Normal 0% baseline)
//   * 20 mA (32000 counts) -> 100 (Full scale 100% LEL or 100 PSI)
// ============================================================================

AI_TempVal (%R00101) := 0;
AI_TempVal (%R00101) := (AI_ValueIn (%R00105) / 32) * 125;
AI_ValueIn (%R00105) := (AI_TempVal (%R00101) / 1000) - 25;
1-to-1 Rung-by-Rung Pseudocode Translation (4 Rungs)
Rung / Source Structured Pseudocode & Ladder Logic
Rung 0
CalcVa1 rung 3 (GE) - BLK_CLR_WORD AI_TempVal %R00120
Source comment: 'Clearing internal register.'. The GE BLK_CLR_WORD block has a single operand, AI_TempVal (%R00120), and zeroes it before the scaling chain runs. Written as MOV(0,AI_TempVal) per the specification's BLK_CLR_WORD -> MOV mapping; Logix CLR(AI_TempVal) is the same operation. !! REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS: the printed BLK_CLR_WORD frame also carries an unlabelled constant '2' in the same position where the MOVE_INT frame of this routine carries '1'; if that digit is the block length N, two words starting at %R00120 are cleared rather than one. Read as a single-register clear because the only operand printed on the block is AI_TempVal (%R00120) and the following register (%R00121) has no entry in var.xml and is referenced nowhere, so a one-word clear is equivalent at symbol level.
AI_TempVal := 0;
MOV(0,AI_TempVal);
Rung 1
CalcVa1 rung 5 (GE) - DIV_INT %R00100/32 -> %R00120 ; MUL_DINT %R00120*125 -> %R00120
Source comment: 'Convert analog input range 0-32000 to 0-125000 range.'. DIV_INT divides AI_ValueIn (%R00100) by the constant 32 into AI_TempVal (%R00120) with IN1=%R00100, IN2=32, Q=%R00120; MUL_DINT then multiplies AI_TempVal by 125 back into AI_TempVal with IN1=%R00120, IN2=125, Q=%R00120. The two steps are kept separate - they are not folded into one rounded expression. The source deliberately uses MUL_DINT for the multiply and DIV_DINT for the next divide because 32000/32*125 = 125000 does not fit a 16-bit register; in Logix both tags are DINT.
AI_TempVal := AI_ValueIn / 32;
AI_TempVal := AI_TempVal * 125;
DIV(AI_ValueIn,32,AI_TempVal)MUL(AI_TempVal,125,AI_TempVal);
Rung 2
CalcVa1 rung 7 (GE) - DIV_DINT %R00120/1000 -> %R00120 ; MOVE_INT %R00120 -> %R00100
Source comment: 'Convert from 125000 range to 125 range. This to display percent value with one desimal.'. DIV_DINT divides AI_TempVal (%R00120) by the constant 1000 into AI_TempVal with IN1=%R00120, IN2=1000, Q=%R00120; MOVE_INT then copies AI_TempVal to AI_ValueIn (%R00100) with IN=%R00120, Q=%R00100.
AI_TempVal := AI_TempVal / 1000;
AI_ValueIn := AI_TempVal;
DIV(AI_TempVal,1000,AI_TempVal)MOV(AI_TempVal,AI_ValueIn);
Rung 3
CalcVa1 rung 9 (GE) - SUB_INT %R00100-25 -> %R00100
Source comment: 'Convert from 0-125 range to -25 to 100 range. This is percent value with one decimal point.'. SUB_INT subtracts the constant 25 from AI_ValueIn (%R00100) with IN1=%R00100, IN2=25 and stores the result back in AI_ValueIn (Q=%R00100).
AI_ValueIn := AI_ValueIn - 25;
SUB(AI_ValueIn,25,AI_ValueIn);

// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: CalcVa3 — Floating-Point Scaling for 0.00..5.00 LELm (DG_7404_011R)
// Source:  LAD/CalcVa3.pdf (2 Rungs)
// Formula: EngVal_Real = (((REAL(RawCounts) / 32.0) * 625.0) / 100000.0) - 1.25
//   * 0.0 mA (    0 counts) -> -1.25000 LELm
//   * 1.5 mA ( 2400 counts) -> -0.78125 LELm (Lower bound of Optical Fault window)
//   * 2.5 mA ( 4000 counts) -> -0.46875 LELm (Upper bound of Optical Fault window)
//   * 4.0 mA ( 6400 counts) ->  0.00000 LELm (Normal 0 LELm baseline)
//   * 20 mA  (32000 counts) ->  5.00000 LELm (Full scale)
// ============================================================================

AI_TempVal_Real (%R00120) := 0.0;
AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00124) := INT_TO_REAL(AI_ValueIn (%R00105));
AI_TempVal_Real (%R00120) := (AI_ValueIn_Real / 32.0) * 625.0;
AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00124) := (AI_TempVal_Real / 100000.0) - 1.25;

⚙ Ai_AL_1 LAD/Ai_AL_1.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 4 L5X Rungs: 4 Called By: AI_1 (All), AI_2 (Ch 9..13, 15..16), AI_3 (Ch 18..22) Calls: None

Standard integer comparator subroutine where both Low Alarm and High Alarm trigger on rising values (>= setpoint). Also evaluates Open Circuit (<= LoFaultSetpoint) and Short Circuit (>= HiFaultSetpoint).

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Ai_AL_1) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Ai_AL_1 — Standard Integer Alarm & Fault Comparators (Rising Lo & Hi)
// Source:  LAD/Ai_AL_1.pdf (4 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

AI_LoAlarm (%M00601) := (AI_ValueIn (%R00105) >= AI_LoAlarmSetpoint (%R00108));  // Rising Low Alarm
AI_HiAlarm (%M00602) := (AI_ValueIn (%R00105) >= AI_HiAlarmSetpoint (%R00106));  // Rising High Alarm
AI_LoFault (%M00603) := (AI_ValueIn (%R00105) <= AI_LoFaultSetpoint (%R00112));  // Open Circuit (Wire Break)
AI_HiFault (%M00604) := (AI_ValueIn (%R00105) >= AI_HiFaultSetpoint (%R00110));  // Short Circuit (Over-range)
1-to-1 Rung-by-Rung Pseudocode Translation (4 Rungs)
Rung / Source Structured Pseudocode & Ladder Logic
Rung 0
Ai_AL_1 rung 2 (GE) - GE_INT AI_ValueIn %R00100 vs AI_LoAlarmSetpoint %R00106 -> COIL AI_LoAlarm %M00600
GE_INT with IN1 = AI_ValueIn (%R00100) and IN2 = AI_LoAlarmSetpoint (%R00106); its Q output drives the coil AI_LoAlarm (%M00600, 'Lo Alarm Out') directly, with no other contact on the rung. GE_INT means the Lo Alarm is TRUE when the converted value is greater than or equal to the Lo alarm setpoint, exactly as the routine header states.
AI_LoAlarm := (AI_ValueIn >= AI_LoAlarmSetpoint);
GEQ(AI_ValueIn,AI_LoAlarmSetpoint)OTE(AI_LoAlarm);
Rung 1
Ai_AL_1 rung 3 (GE) - GE_INT AI_ValueIn %R00100 vs AI_HiAlarmSetpoint %R00108 -> COIL AI_HiAlarm %M00601

AI_HiAlarm := (AI_ValueIn >= AI_HiAlarmSetpoint);
GEQ(AI_ValueIn,AI_HiAlarmSetpoint)OTE(AI_HiAlarm);

LEQ(AI_ValueIn,AI_LoFaultSetpoint)OTE(AI_LoFault);

AI_HiFault := (AI_ValueIn >= AI_HiFaultSetpoint);

GE Rungs: 7 L5X Rungs: 7 Called By: AI_2 (Ch 14: DG_7404_011R Open-Path Gas Detector) Calls: None

Floating-point comparator subroutine for the Open-Path Gas Detector DG_7404_011R. In addition to LoAlarm (>= 1.0 LELm), HiAlarm (>= 3.0 LELm), Open Circuit (<= -0.9 LELm), and Short Circuit (>= 5.5 LELm), Rungs 5..7 check for an Optical Beam Block/Fault window between -0.78125 and -0.46875 LELm (1.5 mA to 2.5 mA).

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Ai_AL_3) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Ai_AL_3 — Floating-Point Alarm, Fault & Optical Window Comparator
// Source:  LAD/Ai_AL_3.pdf (7 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

AI_LoAlarm (%M00601) := (AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00124) >= AI_LoAlarmSetpoint_Real (%R00128));  // >= 1.0 LELm
AI_HiAlarm (%M00602) := (AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00124) >= AI_HiAlarmSetpoint_Real (%R00126));  // >= 3.0 LELm
AI_LoFault (%M00603) := (AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00124) <= AI_LoFaultSetpoint_Real (%R00132));  // <= -0.9 LELm (Open Circuit)
AI_HiFault (%M00604) := (AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00124) >= AI_HiFaultSetpoint_Real (%R00130));  // >= 5.5 LELm (Short Circuit)

// Optical Fault / Beam Obscuration Window (1.5 mA to 2.5 mA = -0.78125 to -0.46875 LELm)
T00011     (%T00011) := (AI_ValueIn_Real <= -0.46875);
T00012     (%T00012) := (AI_ValueIn_Real >= -0.78125);
AI_Fault1  (%M00609) := T00011 AND T00012;

Rung / Source Structured Pseudocode & Ladder Logic
Rung 0
Ai_AL_3 rung 2 (GE) - GE_REAL AI_ValueIn_Real %R00122 vs AI_LoAlarmSetpoint_Real %R00128 -> COIL AI_LoAlarm %M00600
GE_REAL with IN1 = AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00122) and IN2 = AI_LoAlarmSetpoint_Real (%R00128); its Q output drives the coil AI_LoAlarm (%M00600, 'Lo Alarm Out') directly - Lo Alarm TRUE when the converted value is greater than or equal to the Lo alarm setpoint.
AI_LoAlarm := (AI_ValueIn_Real >= AI_LoAlarmSetpoint_Real);
GEQ(AI_ValueIn_Real,AI_LoAlarmSetpoint_Real)OTE(AI_LoAlarm);
Rung 1
Ai_AL_3 rung 3 (GE) - GE_REAL AI_ValueIn_Real %R00122 vs AI_HiAlarmSetpoint_Real %R00126 -> COIL AI_HiAlarm %M00601
GE_REAL with IN1 = AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00122) and IN2 = AI_HiAlarmSetpoint_Real (%R00126); its Q output drives the coil AI_HiAlarm (%M00601, 'Hi Alarm Out') directly - Hi Alarm TRUE when the converted value is greater than or equal to the Hi alarm setpoint.
AI_HiAlarm := (AI_ValueIn_Real >= AI_HiAlarmSetpoint_Real);
GEQ(AI_ValueIn_Real,AI_HiAlarmSetpoint_Real)OTE(AI_HiAlarm);

LE_REAL with IN1 = AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00122) and IN2 = AI_LoFaultSetpoint_Real (%R00130); its Q output drives the coil AI_LoFault (%M00602, 'Lo Fault Out') directly - Lo Fault/Open circuit TRUE when the converted value is less than or equal to the Lo fault setpoint.

LEQ(AI_ValueIn_Real,AI_LoFaultSetpoint_Real)OTE(AI_LoFault);

Ai_AL_3 rung 5 (GE) - GE_REAL AI_ValueIn_Real %R00122 vs AI_HiFaultSetpoint_Real %R00132 -> COIL AI_HiFault %M00604
GE_REAL with IN1 = AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00122) and IN2 = AI_HiFaultSetpoint_Real (%R00132); its Q output drives the coil AI_HiFault (%M00604, 'Hi Fault Out') directly - Hi Fault/Short circuit TRUE when the converted value is greater than or equal to the Hi fault setpoint.

LE_REAL with IN1 = AI_ValueIn_Real (%R00122) and the fixed constant -0.46875 as IN2 (a literal, not a setpoint register); its Q output drives the BOOL bit T00011 (%T00011, 'For Fault 1 comparing on Gas detector') directly. This is the upper edge of the fault-1 window used on rung 8.
T00011 := (AI_ValueIn_Real <= -0.46875);
LEQ(AI_ValueIn_Real,-0.46875)OTE(T00011);

Ai_AL_3 rung 7 (GE) - GE_REAL AI_ValueIn_Real %R00122 vs constant -0.78125 -> COIL T00012 %T00012

GEQ(AI_ValueIn_Real,-0.78125)OTE(T00012);
Rung 6
Ai_AL_3 rung 8 (GE) - NOCON T00011 %T00011 + NOCON T00012 %T00012 -> COIL AI_Fault1 %M00609
Two NO contacts in series: T00011 (%T00011) and T00012 (%T00012), set by rungs 6 and 7, are ANDed to energise AI_Fault1 (%M00609, 'Fault 1 for Gas detecor') - the detector is flagged faulty only while the converted value lies inside the window bounded by -0.78125 and -0.46875.
AI_Fault1 := T00011 AND T00012;
XIC(T00011)XIC(T00012)OTE(AI_Fault1);
5. Analog Channel Processing

⚙ AI_1 LAD/AI_1.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 80 L5X Rungs: 65 Called By: Input Calls: CalcVa1, Ai_AL_1

Processes the first 8 Point IR Gas Detectors (DG_7404_001 through DG_7404_008 on %AI0001..%AI0008). Each detector uses an identical 10-rung template: loads setpoints (Lo=20 %LEL, Hi=60 %LEL, OC=-15, SC=110), scales via CalcVa1, compares via Ai_AL_1, latches Lo/Hi alarms until System_Reset, gates C&E alarms with <Tag>_INH, captures First-Up (<Tag>_FRUP) on High Gas, and outputs Open/Short Circuit faults.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (AI_1) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: AI_1 — Point IR Gas Detectors 001..008 (%AI0001..%AI0008)
// Source:  LAD/AI_1.pdf (80 Rungs — 10 Rungs per Detector)
// Channels:
//   Ch 1 (%AI0001): DG_7404_001 -> %R00001
//   Ch 2 (%AI0002): DG_7404_002 -> %R00002
//   Ch 3 (%AI0003): DG_7404_003 -> %R00003
//   Ch 4 (%AI0004): DG_7404_004 -> %R00004
//   Ch 5 (%AI0005): DG_7404_005 -> %R00005
//   Ch 6 (%AI0006): DG_7404_006 -> %R00006
//   Ch 7 (%AI0007): DG_7404_007 -> %R00007
//   Ch 8 (%AI0008): DG_7404_008 -> %R00008
// ============================================================================

FOR EACH ch IN [DG_7404_001 .. DG_7404_008] DO
    // 1. Load thresholds & scale raw 0..20mA input to -25..100 %LEL
    AI_LoAlarmSetpoint (%R00108) := 20;    // 20 %LEL Low Gas Alarm
    AI_HiAlarmSetpoint (%R00106) := 60;    // 60 %LEL High Gas Alarm
    AI_LoFaultSetpoint (%R00112) := -15;   // Open-Circuit Fault (<= 1.6 mA)
    AI_HiFaultSetpoint (%R00110) := 110;   // Short-Circuit Fault (>= 21.6 mA)

    AI_ValueIn := ch_RAW (%AI000x);
    CALL CalcVa1();
    ch_VAL     := AI_ValueIn;              // Store scaled %LEL for HMI display
    CALL Ai_AL_1();

    // 2. Low Gas Alarm (Latched until System_Reset, gated by channel Inhibit & Faults)
    ch_ALL  := ((AI_LoAlarm OR ch_ALL) AND NOT System_Reset) AND NOT ch_OC AND NOT ch_SC;
    ch_ALLI := ch_ALL AND NOT ch_INH;

    // 3. High Gas Alarm (Latched until System_Reset, gated by channel Inhibit & Faults)
    ch_ALH  := ((AI_HiAlarm OR ch_ALH) AND NOT System_Reset) AND NOT ch_OC AND NOT ch_SC;
    ch_ALHI := ch_ALH AND NOT ch_INH;

    // 4. First-Up Alarm Identification (Captures the very first High Alarm before System_AnyActions sets)
    ch_FRUP := ((ch_ALHI AND NOT System_AnyActions) OR ch_FRUP) AND NOT System_Reset;
    IF ch_FRUP THEN
        LATCH System_AnyActions (%M00701) := TRUE;
    END_IF;

    // 5. Line Fault Outputs (Unlatched, suppressed if channel is Inhibited)
    ch_OC := AI_LoFault AND NOT ch_INH;
    ch_SC := AI_HiFault AND NOT ch_INH;
END_FOR;

// --- 1. Point Gas Detectors DG_7404_009 (%AI0009), DG_7404_010 (%AI0010), and SpareAI_11 (%AI0011) ---
// Same 10-rung template as AI_1 (Lo=20 %LEL, Hi=60 %LEL, OC=-15, SC=110, CalcVa1 + Ai_AL_1)
FOR EACH ch IN [DG_7404_009, DG_7404_010, SpareAI_11] DO
    Process_Standard_Gas_Channel(ch, Lo:=20, Hi:=60, OC:=-15, SC:=110);
END_FOR;

// --- 2. IR Flame Detectors DF_7404_001 (%AI0012) & DF_7404_002 (%AI0013) (Rungs 31..50) ---
// Wired as current-loop discrete sensors; only High Alarm (>= 50) is used for Fire detection.
// Note: High Alarm unlatches on System_Reset OR Pump_Active_1_Hour (%M00621) OR FS_7503_001_ALI (Stop Foam)!
FOR EACH flame IN [DF_7404_001, DF_7404_002] DO
    Setpoints(Lo:=20, Hi:=50, OC:=-15, SC:=110);
    Scale_And_Compare(flame, CalcVa1, Ai_AL_1);
    flame_ALL  := ((AI_LoAlarm OR flame_ALL) AND NOT System_Reset) AND NOT flame_OC AND NOT flame_SC;
    flame_ALLI := flame_ALL AND NOT flame_INH;
    flame_ALH  := ((AI_HiAlarm OR flame_ALH)
                   AND NOT System_Reset
                   AND NOT Pump_Active_1_Hour (%M00621)
                   AND NOT FS_7503_001_ALI    (%M00054))
                  AND NOT flame_OC AND NOT flame_SC;
    flame_ALHI := flame_ALH AND NOT flame_INH;
    Update_FirstUp_And_Faults(flame);
END_FOR;

// --- 3. Open-Path Gas Detector DG_7404_011R (%AI0014) (Rungs 51..61, 11 Rungs) ---
// Uses REAL scaling (CalcVa3: 0.00..5.00 LELm) and Ai_AL_3 (includes Optical Fault FLT1)
AI_LoAlarmSetpoint_Real (%R00128) :=  1.0;   // 1.0 LELm Low Gas
AI_HiAlarmSetpoint_Real (%R00126) :=  3.0;   // 3.0 LELm High Gas
AI_LoFaultSetpoint_Real (%R00132) := -0.9;   // Open Circuit
AI_HiFaultSetpoint_Real (%R00130) :=  5.5;   // Short Circuit
AI_ValueIn := DG_7404_011R (%AI0014);
CALL CalcVa3();
DG_7404_011R_VAL (%R00140) := AI_ValueIn_Real;
CALL Ai_AL_3();
// Alarms are suppressed by OC, SC, or Optical Fault (FLT1)
DG_7404_011R_ALL  := ((AI_LoAlarm OR DG_7404_011R_ALL) AND NOT System_Reset)
                     AND NOT DG_7404_011R_OC AND NOT DG_7404_011R_SC AND NOT DG_7404_011R_FLT1;
DG_7404_011R_ALLI := DG_7404_011R_ALL AND NOT DG_7404_011R_INH;
DG_7404_011R_ALH  := ((AI_HiAlarm OR DG_7404_011R_ALH) AND NOT System_Reset)
                     AND NOT DG_7404_011R_OC AND NOT DG_7404_011R_SC AND NOT DG_7404_011R_FLT1;
DG_7404_011R_ALHI := DG_7404_011R_ALH AND NOT DG_7404_011R_INH;
Update_FirstUp(DG_7404_011R);
DG_7404_011R_OC   := AI_LoFault AND NOT DG_7404_011R_INH;
DG_7404_011R_SC   := AI_HiFault AND NOT DG_7404_011R_INH;
DG_7404_011R_FLT1 := AI_Fault1  AND NOT DG_7404_011R_INH;  // Rung 61: Beam Block / Optical Fault

// --- 4. Spare Channels SpareAI_15 (%AI0015) & SpareAI_16 (%AI0016) (Rungs 62..81) ---
FOR EACH sp IN [SpareAI_15, SpareAI_16] DO
    Process_Standard_Channel(sp, Lo:=20, Hi:=50, OC:=-15, SC:=110);
END_FOR;

5. Analog Channel Processing

⚙ AI_3 LAD/AI_3.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 63 L5X Rungs: 48 Called By: Input Calls: CalcVa1, CalcVa2, Ai_AL_1, Ai_AL_2

Processes Analog Input Card 3 (%AI0017..%AI0022): Air Accumulator Pressure PST_7002_001 (falling low alarm <= 50 PSI), Fuel Gas Pressure PST_6401_001 (0..150 PSI, high alarm >= 100 PSI), Deluge Line Pressure PST_7503_001 (unlatched high pressure status >= 50 PSI confirming deluge release), and Monitored Foam Release Pushbuttons FR_7503_001_002 (Field) & FR_7503_003 (Panel).

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (AI_3) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: AI_3 — Pressure Transmitters & Monitored Foam Pushbuttons (%AI0017..%AI0022)
// Source:  LAD/AI_3.pdf (63 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// --- 1. PST_7002_001 (%AI0017): ESDV Air Accumulator Pressure (0..100 PSI, Rungs 1..10) ---
// Uses CalcVa1 and Ai_AL_2 (FALLING Low Alarm when pressure drops <= 50 PSI)
// First-Up is triggered by Low Alarm (PST_7002_001_ALLI) instead of High Alarm!
Setpoints(Lo:=50, Hi:=50, OC:=-15, SC:=110);
Scale_And_Compare(PST_7002_001, CalcVa1, Ai_AL_2);
PST_7002_001_ALL  := ((AI_LoAlarm OR PST_7002_001_ALL) AND NOT System_Reset) AND NOT PST_7002_001_OC AND NOT PST_7002_001_SC;
PST_7002_001_ALLI := PST_7002_001_ALL AND NOT PST_7002_001_INH;  // Low Air Pressure -> Tag_DO_14 Lamp

// --- 2. PST_6401_001 (%AI0018): Fuel Gas Pressure (0..150 PSI, Rungs 11..20) ---
// Uses CalcVa2 (-37..150 PSI) and Ai_AL_1; High Pressure >= 100 PSI triggers ESD & Fuel Gas Shutdown
Setpoints(Lo:=30, Hi:=100, OC:=-22, SC:=165);
Scale_And_Compare(PST_6401_001, CalcVa2, Ai_AL_1);
PST_6401_001_ALH  := ((AI_HiAlarm OR PST_6401_001_ALH) AND NOT System_Reset) AND NOT PST_6401_001_OC AND NOT PST_6401_001_SC;
PST_6401_001_ALHI := PST_6401_001_ALH AND NOT PST_6401_001_INH;

// --- 3. PST_7503_001 (%AI0019): Deluge System Line Pressure (0..100 PSI, Rungs 21..30) ---
// UNLATCHED alarms: PST_7503_001_ALHI (>= 50 PSI) indicates water/foam pressure is established,
// which cancels the Standby Pump B start sequence in CE_LOG.
Setpoints(Lo:=30, Hi:=50, OC:=-15, SC:=102);
Scale_And_Compare(PST_7503_001, CalcVa1, Ai_AL_1);
PST_7503_001_ALL  := AI_LoAlarm AND NOT System_Reset AND NOT PST_7503_001_OC AND NOT PST_7503_001_SC; // Unlatched
PST_7503_001_ALH  := AI_HiAlarm AND NOT System_Reset AND NOT PST_7503_001_OC AND NOT PST_7503_001_SC; // Unlatched
PST_7503_001_ALHI := PST_7503_001_ALH AND NOT PST_7503_001_INH;

// --- 4. FR_7503_001_002 (%AI0020) & FR_7503_003 (%AI0022): Foam Release Pushbuttons (Rungs 31..40, 51..60) ---
// Wired with end-of-line & contact resistors on 4..20mA loops for line-fault supervision.
// High Alarm (>= 50) unlatches on System_Reset OR Pump_Active_1_Hour OR FS_7503_001_ALI (Stop Foam).
FOR EACH pb IN [FR_7503_001_002, FR_7503_003] DO
    Setpoints(Lo:=20, Hi:=50, OC:=-15, SC:=110);
    Scale_And_Compare(pb, CalcVa1, Ai_AL_1);
    pb_ALH  := ((AI_HiAlarm OR pb_ALH)
                AND NOT System_Reset
                AND NOT Pump_Active_1_Hour (%M00621)
                AND NOT FS_7503_001_ALI    (%M00054))
               AND NOT pb_OC AND NOT pb_SC;
    pb_ALHI := pb_ALH AND NOT pb_INH;
    // NOTE: In original GE AI_3.pdf Rung 60, FR_7503_003_FRUP accidentally checks SpareAI_21_ALHI (copy-paste quirk)
END_FOR;

6. Detector & System Voting

⚙ Vote_1 LAD/Vote_1.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 4 L5X Rungs: 4 Called By: Input Calls: None

Aggregates individual channel statuses into 4 system-wide summary flags: Point Gas Low Alarm Voting (%M00605), Point Gas High Alarm Voting (%M00606), Any Channel Inhibited (%M00607 across 56 channels), and Any Channel Fault (%M00608 across 81 OC/SC/FLT1 bits).

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Vote_1) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Vote_1 — Gas Detector Voting, Inhibit Summary & Fault Summary
// Source:  LAD/Vote_1.pdf (4 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// Rung 1: Point IR Gas Detectors Low Alarm Voting (DG_7404_001 .. DG_7404_010)
// Note: Cause & Effect Matrix specifies SINGLE (1oo10) detection.
Voting_DG_7404_ALLI (%M00605) :=
    DG_7404_001_ALLI OR DG_7404_002_ALLI OR DG_7404_003_ALLI OR DG_7404_004_ALLI OR DG_7404_005_ALLI OR
    DG_7404_006_ALLI OR DG_7404_007_ALLI OR DG_7404_008_ALLI OR DG_7404_009_ALLI OR DG_7404_010_ALLI;

// Rung 2: Point IR Gas Detectors High Alarm Voting (DG_7404_001 .. DG_7404_010) -> Triggers ESD
Voting_DG_7404_ALHI (%M00606) :=
    DG_7404_001_ALHI OR DG_7404_002_ALHI OR DG_7404_003_ALHI OR DG_7404_004_ALHI OR DG_7404_005_ALHI OR
    DG_7404_006_ALHI OR DG_7404_007_ALHI OR DG_7404_008_ALHI OR DG_7404_009_ALHI OR DG_7404_010_ALHI;

// Rung 3: System-Wide Inhibit Summary (OR of all 56 <Tag>_INH bits across DI_1, DI_2, AI_1, AI_2, AI_3)
Voting_All_Inhibits (%M00607) :=
    (ANY of the 32 Discrete Input _INH bits %M00002..%M00095 is TRUE) OR
    (ANY of the 24 Analog Input _INH bits   %M00303..%M00441 is TRUE);

// Rung 4: System-Wide Line Fault Summary (OR of all 81 Open-Circuit, Short-Circuit & Optical Fault bits)
Voting_All_Faults (%M00608) :=
    (ANY Discrete Input _OC / _SC bit is TRUE) OR
    (ANY Analog Input _OC / _SC bit %M00305..%M00444 is TRUE) OR
    DG_7404_011R_FLT1 (%M00610) OR
    PUMP_A_OC (%M00293) OR PUMP_B_START_OC (%M00295);

7. Core Logic, Startup & Cause-and-Effect

⚙ Logic LAD/Logic.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 14 L5X Rungs: 20 Called By: _MAIN Calls: CE_LOG (after 120s warmup), Sound (every scan)

Manages System Reset (from HMI button or automatic startup reset), clears PLC/IO fault tables via SVC_REQ 14, enforces a 120-second detector stabilization warmup delay (T00002) on PLC power-up before enabling Cause & Effect (CE_LOG), pulses an automatic reset during the final 2 seconds of warmup, and calls Sound.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Logic) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Logic — System Reset, 120s Startup Stabilization & C&E Dispatcher
// Source:  LAD/Logic.pdf (14 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// --- 1. Master System Reset & 5.0s HMI Reset Button Auto-Release (Rungs 1..4) ---
System_Reset (%M00700) := System_Reset_HMI (%M00703) OR System_Reset_Startup (%M00702);

System_Reset_HMI_Help (%M00705) := RISING_EDGE(System_Reset_HMI);
ONDTR_TIMER(System_HMI_Reset_Timer (%R00199),
            Enable := System_Reset_HMI,
            Reset  := System_Reset_HMI_Help,
            Preset := 5.0 s (50 tenths)) -> T00001 (%T00001);
// Keep System_Reset_HMI latched until the 5.0s timer finishes, then auto-clear it:
System_Reset_HMI (%M00703) := System_Reset_HMI AND NOT T00001;

// --- 2. Clear PLC & I/O Hardware Fault Tables on System_Reset (Rungs 5..8) ---
IF System_Reset (%M00700) THEN
    System_ClearPLC_Fault (%R00201) := 0;
    SVC_REQ(14, System_ClearPLC_Fault);  // Clear PLC CPU Fault Table
    System_ClearIO_Fault  (%R00200) := 0;
    SVC_REQ(14, System_ClearIO_Fault);   // Clear I/O Fault Table
    UNLATCH System_AnyActions (%M00701) := FALSE;
END_IF;

// --- 3. 120.0-Second Startup Sensor Stabilization Timer (Rungs 9..11) ---
// Prevents false trips while gas/flame detectors warm up after PLC power-on.
ONDTR_TIMER(System_C_E_Delay (%R00202),
            Enable := TRUE,
            Reset  := #ALW_OFF (%S00008),
            Preset := 120.0 s (1200 tenths)) -> T00002 (%T00002);

IF NOT T00002 THEN
    // Compute remaining warmup time in tenths of a second (1200 - Elapsed)
    System_Reset_HelpRegister (%R00232) := System_C_E_Delay.PV (1200) - System_C_E_Delay.CV;
    // During the final 2.0 seconds of warmup (<= 20 tenths left), pulse System_Reset_Startup
    // to clear all alarms latched during sensor power-up!
    System_Reset_Startup (%M00702) := (System_Reset_HelpRegister <= 20);
ELSE
    System_Reset_Startup (%M00702) := FALSE;
END_IF;

// --- 4. Execute Cause & Effect (Only After 120s Warmup) and Sound (Every Scan) (Rungs 13..14) ---
IF T00002 (%T00002) THEN
    CALL CE_LOG();
END_IF;

IF NOT #FST_SCN (%S00001) THEN
    CALL Sound();
END_IF;
1-to-1 Rung-by-Rung Pseudocode Translation (20 Rungs)
Rung / Source Structured Pseudocode & Ladder Logic
Rung 0
Logic - ADDED helper (no GE print), free-running self-resetting TON for #T_SEC %S00005
Added rung: the VersaMax supplied #T_SEC (%S00005) as a CPU system bit; RSLogix 5000 v17 has no equivalent, so it is generated here. TMR_T_SEC is a self-resetting TON - while its own .DN is clear the rung is true and the timer ramps from 0 to 1000 ms, then .DN makes the rung false and the timer resets itself, giving an exact 1 s ramp. The 0.5 s on / 0.5 s off square wave is taken from the accumulator in the next rung.
IF NOT TMR_T_SEC.DN THEN
    TON_TIMER(TMR_T_SEC, Preset := 1 s);  // 1000 ms
END_IF;
XIO(TMR_T_SEC.DN)TON(TMR_T_SEC,1000,0);
Rung 1
Logic - ADDED helper (no GE print), T_SEC_PULSE derivation from TMR_T_SEC.ACC
Added rung: T_SEC_PULSE is the replacement for #T_SEC (%S00005) and must be 0.5 s TRUE / 0.5 s off. Because the 1 s ramp above runs 0..1000 ms, .ACC < 500 is TRUE for the first 500 ms of every second, which is exactly the 0.5 s on / 0.5 s off duty cycle. Same polarity and period as the GE system bit.
#T_SEC%S00005 := (TMR_T_SEC.ACC < 500);
LES(TMR_T_SEC.ACC,500)OTE(T_SEC_PULSE);
Rung 2
Logic - ADDED helper (no GE print), free-running self-resetting TON for #T_MIN %S00006
Added rung: the VersaMax supplied #T_MIN (%S00006) as a CPU system bit. TMR_T_MIN is a self-resetting TON with a 60000 ms preset, so it free-runs 0..60000 ms and restarts itself on its own .DN, giving an exact 1 minute ramp.
IF NOT TMR_T_MIN.DN THEN
    TON_TIMER(TMR_T_MIN, Preset := 60 s);  // 60000 ms
END_IF;
XIO(TMR_T_MIN.DN)TON(TMR_T_MIN,60000,0);
Rung 3
Logic - ADDED helper (no GE print), T_MIN_PULSE derivation from TMR_T_MIN.ACC
Added rung: T_MIN_PULSE is the replacement for #T_MIN (%S00006) and must be 30 s TRUE / 30 s off. With the 60 s ramp above, .ACC < 30000 is TRUE for the first 30 s of every minute, exactly the 30 s on / 30 s off duty cycle of the GE system bit.
#T_MIN%S00006 := (TMR_T_MIN.ACC < 30000);
LES(TMR_T_MIN.ACC,30000)OTE(T_MIN_PULSE);
Rung 4
Logic rung 3 (GE) - NOCON System_Reset_HMI %M00703 parallel NOCON System_Reset_Startup %M00702 -> COIL System_Reset %M00700
Calculating system reset. The two NO contacts sit on two branch rows joined by the BUS at x=91, so they are OR-ed: System_Reset_HMI (%M00703, reset activation from the HMI panel) OR System_Reset_Startup (%M00702, used to reset the system at startup) drives the unlatched coil System_Reset (%M00700, 'Reset all latches'). The commented-out BUS at x=663 is the coil's own wire, no further branch.
System_Reset := (System_Reset_HMI OR System_Reset_Startup);
[XIC(System_Reset_HMI),XIC(System_Reset_Startup)]OTE(System_Reset);
Rung 5
Logic rung 4 (GE) - NOCON System_Reset_HMI %M00703 -> POSCOIL System_Reset_HMI_Help %M00704
Positive-transition coil: the two diagonals above the coil circle in the print are the POSCOIL chevron. On the rising edge of System_Reset_HMI (%M00703) the helper bit System_Reset_HMI_Help (%M00704, 'Help puls from HMI (panel) reset signal') pulses TRUE for one scan. The edge is stored in System_Reset_HMI_Help_OS (declared in tags_extra).
System_Reset_HMI_Help := RISING_EDGE(System_Reset_HMI);  // One-Shot Pulse (POSCOIL)
XIC(System_Reset_HMI)ONS(System_Reset_HMI_Help_OS)OTE(System_Reset_HMI_Help);
Rung 6
Logic rung 5 (GE) part 1/3 - NOCON System_Reset_HMI %M00703 into ONDTR TENTHS System_HMI_Reset_Timer %R00205, PV 50 tenths
The 5 second HMI reset timer. System_Reset_HMI (%M00703) is the rung condition into the ONDTR TENTHS block whose register is System_HMI_Reset_Timer (%R00205) and whose printed PV is 50 tenths, i.e. 5000 ms. The R pin on the lower branch row (System_Reset_HMI_Help %M00704) becomes a separate RES rung (part 3/3) because a Logix TON has no reset pin. !! REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS: rung 5 is a self-referential negated coil - the NCCOIL writes System_Reset_HMI (%M00703) while the same bit is the rung's own input contact. The negated coil is therefore implemented as the inverted output of the block (XIO of the timer done in part 2/3) with the source contact polarity left as XIC, which is the only reading that still gives the documented behaviour ('HMI reset bit is reset after 5 sec.'). Second ambiguity: the GE ONDTR is a RETENTIVE on-delay, whereas the mapping rule makes it a plain Logix TON; with a non-retentive TON the negated output would restart the timer as soon as it drops %M00703, so a Logix RTO would reproduce the source exactly. TON was used to follow the mandated ONDTR_TENTHS -> TON mapping.
IF System_Reset_HMI THEN
    TON_TIMER(TMR_HMI_Reset(%R00205), Preset := 5 s);  // 5000 ms
END_IF;
XIC(System_Reset_HMI)TON(TMR_HMI_Reset,5000,0);
Rung 7
Logic rung 5 (GE) part 2/3 - negated coil (NCCOIL) System_Reset_HMI %M00703 driven by the ONDTR Q output
The printed coil is a negated coil (diagonal slash across the circle, xref NCCOIL). Its output is the inverse of the rung condition, so it is written as XIO of the timer done bit: while the 5 s timer is not done System_Reset_HMI (%M00703) is held TRUE, and 5000 ms after the press it is driven FALSE, which is exactly 'HMI reset bit is reset after 5 sec.'. The source contact polarity is untouched (it stayed XIC in part 1/3).
System_Reset_HMI := NOT TMR_HMI_Reset(%R00205).DN;
XIO(TMR_HMI_Reset.DN)OTE(System_Reset_HMI);
Rung 8
Logic rung 5 (GE) part 3/3 - NOCON System_Reset_HMI_Help %M00704 to the ONDTR R pin
The ONDTR R (reset) pin is fed from the branch row through the NO contact System_Reset_HMI_Help (%M00704), the one-shot produced by rung 4. A Logix TON has no R pin, so the same contact drives a RES instruction on the timer, which clears the 5 s accumulation each time a new HMI press is edge-detected.
IF System_Reset_HMI_Help THEN
    RESET(TMR_HMI_Reset(%R00205));
END_IF;
XIC(System_Reset_HMI_Help)RES(TMR_HMI_Reset);
Rung 9
Logic rung 7 (GE) part 1/2 - NOCON System_Reset %M00700 -> MOVE WORD 0 into System_ClearPLC_Fault %R00200
CLEAR PLC FAULT TABLE. MOVE WORD with IN = constant 0 and Q = System_ClearPLC_Fault (%R00200), executed only while System_Reset (%M00700) is TRUE: the helper register is cleared to 0 every scan the system is being reset, ready for the SVC REQ that follows.
IF System_Reset THEN
    System_ClearPLC_Fault := 0;
END_IF;
XIC(System_Reset)MOV(0,System_ClearPLC_Fault);
Rung 10
Logic rung 7 (GE) part 2/2 - NOCON System_Reset %M00700 -> SVC REQ FNC=14, PRM System_ClearPLC_Fault %R00200
Second block of the same printed rung: SVC REQ with FNC = 14 and the PRM parameter register System_ClearPLC_Fault (%R00200). It is enabled by the same System_Reset (%M00700) contact as the MOVE WORD, so the service request is issued on every scan in which the reset is active. Split into its own rung because Logix v17 allows only one output instruction per rung.
IF System_Reset THEN
    SVC_REQ(Code := 14, Param := System_ClearPLC_Fault);  // Clear Fault Table
END_IF;
XIC(System_Reset)SVC(14,System_ClearPLC_Fault);
Rung 11
Logic rung 9 (GE) part 1/2 - NOCON System_Reset %M00700 -> MOVE WORD 0 into System_ClearIO_Fault %R00201
CLEAR IO FAULT TABLE. Same structure as rung 7 with the other helper register: MOVE WORD clears System_ClearIO_Fault (%R00201) to 0 while System_Reset (%M00700) is TRUE.
IF System_Reset THEN
    System_ClearIO_Fault := 0;
END_IF;
XIC(System_Reset)MOV(0,System_ClearIO_Fault);
Rung 12
Logic rung 9 (GE) part 2/2 - NOCON System_Reset %M00700 -> SVC REQ FNC=14, PRM System_ClearIO_Fault %R00201
SVC REQ with FNC = 14 and PRM = System_ClearIO_Fault (%R00201), gated by the same System_Reset (%M00700) contact, issuing the I/O fault table clear. Kept as a separate rung for the single-output-per-rung rule.
IF System_Reset THEN
    SVC_REQ(Code := 14, Param := System_ClearIO_Fault);  // Clear Fault Table
END_IF;
XIC(System_Reset)SVC(14,System_ClearIO_Fault);
Rung 13
Logic rung 11 (GE) part 1/3 - NOCON #ALW_ON %S00007 into ONDTR TENTHS System_C_E_Delay %R00202, PV 1200 tenths
Calculating the delay before C&E is called: the 2 minute Cause & Effect start-up delay. #ALW_ON (%S00007) is an always-true system bit, so per the mapping rules the contact is dropped and the block runs unconditionally. The ONDTR TENTHS register is System_C_E_Delay (%R00202) with the printed PV of 1200 tenths, i.e. 120000 ms (120 s). The R pin is the always-off bit #ALW_OFF, handled in part 3/3.
TON_TIMER(TMR_C_E_Delay(%R00202), Preset := 120 s);  // 120000 ms
TON(TMR_C_E_Delay,120000,0);
Rung 14
Logic rung 11 (GE) part 2/3 - ONDTR Q output -> COIL T00002 %T00002
The block's Q output drives the coil T00002 (%T00002, 'High 120 sec. after PLC set in run.'). T00002 is a plain BOOL flag in the symbol table (it is written by an ordinary coil, not by the timer block), so it stays a BOOL tag; it mirrors the 120 s done bit and is the contact used by rungs 13 and 15.
T00002 := TMR_C_E_Delay(%R00202).DN;
XIC(TMR_C_E_Delay.DN)OTE(T00002);
Rung 15
Logic rung 11 (GE) part 3/3 - NOCON #ALW_OFF %S00008 to the ONDTR R pin
The ONDTR R pin is wired to #ALW_OFF (%S00008, 'Always OFF') on the branch row, i.e. the retentive delay timer is deliberately never reset and counts up once after the PLC enters RUN. Because a Logix TON has no reset pin this is written as a RES rung gated by the always-false bit SYS_ALW_OFF (declared in tags_extra, permanently 0), so the reset can never fire - identical behaviour to the source.
IF SYS_ALW_OFF(%S00008) THEN
    RESET(TMR_C_E_Delay(%R00202));
END_IF;
XIC(SYS_ALW_OFF)RES(TMR_C_E_Delay);
Rung 16
Logic rung 13 (GE) part 1/2 - NCCON T00002 %T00002 -> SUB INT System_C_E_Delay[1
%R00203 minus System_C_E_Delay[0] %R00202 into System_Reset_HelpRegister %R00208] Reset the system 2 seconds before the 120 sec timer is finnish. While T00002 (%T00002) is FALSE the SUB INT block runs with IN1 = System_C_E_Delay[1] (%R00203) and IN2 = System_C_E_Delay[0] (%R00202) and puts IN1 - IN2 into System_Reset_HelpRegister (%R00208). In the GE timer register [1] holds the preset (1200) and [0] the running accumulator, so the difference is the time still left before the 120 s delay expires.
IF NOT T00002 THEN
    System_Reset_HelpRegister := System_C_E_Delay[1] - System_C_E_Delay[0];
END_IF;
XIO(T00002)SUB(System_C_E_Delay[1],System_C_E_Delay[0],System_Reset_HelpRegister);
Rung 17
Logic rung 13 (GE) part 2/2 - LE INT System_Reset_HelpRegister %R00208 vs 20 -> COIL System_Reset_Startup %M00702
The LE INT block of the same printed rung has IN1 = System_Reset_HelpRegister (%R00208) and IN2 = constant 20, so its Q is TRUE when the remaining time is less than or equal to 20 tenths (2 s), and that drives the coil System_Reset_Startup (%M00702). Gated by the same NC T00002 (%T00002) contact; when the 120 s flag is set the coil is written FALSE. Because SUB runs first in scan order the compare always sees this scan's result.
System_Reset_Startup := NOT T00002 AND (System_Reset_HelpRegister <= 20);
XIO(T00002)LEQ(System_Reset_HelpRegister,20)OTE(System_Reset_Startup);
Rung 18
Logic rung 15 (GE) - NOCON T00002 %T00002 -> CALL CE_LOG
Calling Cause & Effect logic. Once the 120 s start-up delay flag T00002 (%T00002) is TRUE the conditional CALL block invokes the CE_LOG routine on every scan. The #ALW_ON style always-true contact is not present here, so the JSR is gated only by T00002.
IF T00002 THEN
    CALL CE_LOG();
END_IF;
XIC(T00002)JSR(CE_LOG,0);
Rung 19
Logic rung 16 (GE) - NCCON #FST_SCN %S00001 -> CALL Sound
The NC contact #FST_SCN (%S00001, 'Set to 1 when the current sweep is the first sweep') suppresses the CALL to the Sound routine on the very first scan; from the second scan onwards JSR Sound runs unconditionally. #FST_SCN maps to the Logix status bit S:FS, so the contact becomes XIO(S:FS).
IF NOT #FST_SCN%S00001 THEN
    CALL Sound();
END_IF;
XIO(S:FS)JSR(Sound,0);
7. Core Logic, Startup & Cause-and-Effect

⚙ CE_LOG LAD/CE_LOG.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 11 L5X Rungs: 24 Called By: Logic (when T00002 = TRUE after 120s startup delay) Calls: None

Implements the Cause & Effect Matrix (DE-GN-FG-SAF-74-1001): trips Main & Booster Pumps on Confirmed Gas, Flame, Foam Release, High Fuel Gas Pressure, or ESDV closure; isolates the Fuel Gas ESDV; controls Duty Electric Foam Pump A (with 1-hour max runtime counter); runs the 3-attempt Standby Diesel Pump B automatic start sequence if deluge pressure (< 50 PSI) fails to build within 30s; generates a 2s Pump B stop pulse; and drives ESDV status lamp flags.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (CE_LOG) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: CE_LOG — Cause & Effect Matrix & Deluge Pump Sequencing
// Source:  LAD/CE_LOG.pdf (11 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// --- Rung 1: Main & Booster Pump Shutdown Command (9 Trip Causes) ---
Pump_Trip_Demand :=
    Voting_DG_7404_ALHI  (%M00606) OR  // High Gas on any Point Detector (001..010)
    DG_7404_011R_ALHI    (%M00523) OR  // High Gas on Open-Path Detector (011R)
    DF_7404_001_ALHI     (%M00499) OR  // Flame Detector 001 Fire Alarm
    DF_7404_002_ALHI     (%M00500) OR  // Flame Detector 002 Fire Alarm
    FR_7503_001_002_ALHI (%M00535) OR  // Field Manual Foam Release Pushbutton
    FR_7503_003_ALHI     (%M00539) OR  // Panel Manual Foam Release Pushbutton
    PST_6401_001_ALHI    (%M00531) OR  // High Fuel Gas Pressure (>= 100 PSI)
    ZSL_6401_001_ALI     (%M00053) OR  // Fuel Gas ESD Valve Closed Limit Switch
    ESDV_6401_001_ALI    (%M00061);    // Manual ESD Fuel Gas Pushbutton

P2100_P2200_INT  (%M00203) := Pump_Trip_Demand;  // Oil Booster Pumps Shutdown
P3600_P3700_INT  (%M00204) := Pump_Trip_Demand;  // Water Booster Pumps Shutdown
PumpShutdown_INT (%M00208) := Pump_Trip_Demand;  // Main Power Oil & Water Injection Pumps Shutdown

// --- Rung 2: Fuel Gas ESD Solenoid Valve Trip Command (7 Trip Causes) ---
EY_6401_001_002_INT (%M00201) :=
    Voting_DG_7404_ALHI  OR DG_7404_011R_ALHI    OR
    DF_7404_001_ALHI     OR DF_7404_002_ALHI     OR
    FR_7503_001_002_ALHI OR FR_7503_003_ALHI     OR
    PST_6401_001_ALHI;

// --- Rung 3: Duty Electric Deluge Pump A Start/Stop Latch ---
// Starts on Flame or Manual Foam Release; stops on Stop Foam button (FS_7503_001_ALI),
// System_Reset, or after 1 continuous hour of operation (Pump_Active_1_Hour).
PUMP_A_INT (%M00205) :=
    (DF_7404_001_ALHI OR DF_7404_002_ALHI OR FR_7503_001_002_ALHI OR FR_7503_003_ALHI OR PUMP_A_INT)
    AND NOT FS_7503_001_ALI    (%M00054)   // Stop Foam Release pushbutton (NCCON in GE PDF)
    AND NOT System_Reset       (%M00700)
    AND NOT Pump_Active_1_Hour (%M00621);

// --- Rung 4: 1-Hour (3600 Seconds) Maximum Run-Time Counter for Deluge Pump A ---
COUNT_UP(Register := %R00226,
         Clock    := PUMP_A_INT AND #T_SEC (%S00005),
         Reset    := FS_7503_001_ALI OR System_Reset OR Pump_Active_1_Hour,
         Preset   := 3600) -> Pump_Active_1_Hour (%M00621);

// --- Rung 5: Standby Diesel Deluge Pump B — 3-Attempt Start Sequence ---
// If Pump A is commanded ON (PUMP_A_INT = 1) but Deluge Pressure PST_7503_001_ALHI (< 50 PSI)
// is NOT achieved within 30s, issue up to three 2-second start pulses spaced 60s apart:
//   * Attempt 1: t =  30.0s ..  32.0s  (T00003=1, T00004=0)
//   * Attempt 2: t =  92.0s ..  94.0s  (T00005=1, T00006=0)
//   * Attempt 3: t = 154.0s .. 156.0s  (T00007=1, T00008=0)
// All timers reset immediately if PST_7503_001_ALHI (>= 50 PSI) turns ON!
Reset_Deluge_Start := PST_7503_001_ALHI (%M00533);
ONDTR(Pump_Timer1, Enable := PUMP_A_INT, Reset := Reset_Deluge_Start, PV := 30.0s) -> T00003;
ONDTR(Pump_Timer2, Enable := T00003,     Reset := Reset_Deluge_Start, PV :=  2.0s) -> T00004;
ONDTR(Pump_Timer3, Enable := T00004,     Reset := Reset_Deluge_Start, PV := 60.0s) -> T00005;
ONDTR(Pump_Timer4, Enable := T00005,     Reset := Reset_Deluge_Start, PV :=  2.0s) -> T00006;
ONDTR(Pump_Timer5, Enable := T00006,     Reset := Reset_Deluge_Start, PV := 60.0s) -> T00007;
ONDTR(Pump_Timer6, Enable := T00007,     Reset := Reset_Deluge_Start, PV :=  2.0s) -> T00008;

PUMP_B_START_INT (%M00207) :=
    (T00003 AND NOT T00004) OR   // Pulse 1 (2.0 s)
    (T00005 AND NOT T00006) OR   // Pulse 2 (2.0 s)
    (T00007 AND NOT T00008);     // Pulse 3 (2.0 s)

// --- Rung 6: Standby Diesel Pump B Stop Pulse (2.0s Pulse when Fire/Foam Clears or Stop Pressed) ---
No_Fire_Or_Foam := NOT DF_7404_001_ALHI AND NOT DF_7404_002_ALHI
                   AND NOT FR_7503_001_002_ALHI AND NOT FR_7503_003_ALHI;
ONDTR(Pump_Timer8, Enable := No_Fire_Or_Foam OR FS_7503_001_ALI, Reset := FALSE, PV := 2.0s) -> T00009;
PUMP_B_STOP_INT (%M00206) := (No_Fire_Or_Foam AND NOT T00009) OR FS_7503_001_ALI;

// --- Rung 7: Deluge Failed To Release Alarm (60s after 3rd Pump B Start Pulse Completes) ---
ONDTR(Pump_Timer7, Enable := T00008, Reset := PST_7503_001_ALHI, PV := 60.0s) -> DelugeFailedToRelease (%M00620);

// --- Rungs 9..11: ESD Valve Panel Indicator Lamp Commands ---

7. Core Logic, Startup & Cause-and-Effect

⚙ Sound LAD/Sound.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 50 L5X Rungs: 45 Called By: Logic Calls: None

Manages audible alarm annunciation for the PCR Control Panel Buzzer (Tag_DO_15_INT), Pump House Local Horn/Bell (SA_7404_001_002_INT), and PLC Fault Buzzer (PLC_Fault_INT). Uses 38 rising-edge one-shot coils (POSCOIL System_Sound01..37, 40) so that any new alarm re-triggers the sounder after an operator presses System_Mute.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Sound) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Sound — Rising-Edge Audible Alarm Latching & Mute Logic
// Source:  LAD/Sound.pdf (50 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// --- Rungs 1..38: Rising-Edge One-Shot Detection (POSCOIL) on Each Alarm Source ---
// Group A (System_Sound01..26): Process, Fire, Gas, Inhibit & Line Fault Alarms
//   -> Triggers BOTH PCR Panel Buzzer (Tag_DO_15_INT) AND Pump House Horn (SA_7404_001_002_INT)
System_Sound01 := RISING_EDGE(Voting_DG_7404_ALLI);    // Point Gas Low
System_Sound02 := RISING_EDGE(Voting_DG_7404_ALHI);    // Point Gas High
System_Sound03 := RISING_EDGE(Voting_All_Inhibits);    // Any Channel Inhibited
System_Sound04 := RISING_EDGE(Voting_All_Faults);      // Any Channel Fault
System_Sound05 := RISING_EDGE(DG_7404_011R_ALLI);      // Open-Path Gas Low
System_Sound06 := RISING_EDGE(DG_7404_011R_ALHI);      // Open-Path Gas High
System_Sound07 := RISING_EDGE(DF_7404_001_ALHI);       // Flame Detector 001
System_Sound08 := RISING_EDGE(DF_7404_002_ALHI);       // Flame Detector 002
System_Sound09 := RISING_EDGE(PST_7002_001_ALLI);      // ESDV Air Pressure Low
System_Sound10 := RISING_EDGE(PST_6401_001_ALHI);      // Fuel Gas Pressure High
System_Sound11 := RISING_EDGE(PST_7503_001_ALHI);      // Deluge Line Pressure High (Released)
System_Sound12 := RISING_EDGE(FR_7503_001_002_ALHI);   // Field Foam Release Pushbutton
System_Sound13 := RISING_EDGE(FR_7503_003_ALHI);       // Panel Foam Release Pushbutton
System_Sound14 := RISING_EDGE(ZSL_6401_001_ALI);       // ESD Valve Closed
System_Sound15 := RISING_EDGE(FS_7503_001_ALI);        // Stop Foam Button Pressed
System_Sound16 := RISING_EDGE(LS_7503_001_ALI);        // AFFF Tank Low Level
System_Sound17 := RISING_EDGE(LS_7503_002_ALI);        // Diesel Tank Low Level
System_Sound18 := RISING_EDGE(ESDV_6401_001_ALI);      // ESD Fuel Gas Button Pressed
System_Sound19 := RISING_EDGE(SpareDI_11_ALI);         // Spare DI 11
System_Sound20 := RISING_EDGE(SpareAI_11_ALLI);        // Spare AI 11 Lo
System_Sound21 := RISING_EDGE(SpareAI_11_ALHI);        // Spare AI 11 Hi
System_Sound22 := RISING_EDGE(SpareAI_15_ALLI);        // Spare AI 15 Lo
System_Sound23 := RISING_EDGE(SpareAI_15_ALHI);        // Spare AI 15 Hi
System_Sound24 := RISING_EDGE(SpareAI_16_ALLI);        // Spare AI 16 Lo
System_Sound25 := RISING_EDGE(SpareAI_16_ALHI);        // Spare AI 16 Hi
System_Sound26 := RISING_EDGE(INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI);   // Inhibit Foam Release Keyswitch

// Group B (System_Sound27..31): Triggers PCR Panel Buzzer (Tag_DO_15_INT) ONLY
System_Sound27 := RISING_EDGE(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI);
System_Sound28 := RISING_EDGE(SpareAI_21_ALLI);
System_Sound29 := RISING_EDGE(SpareAI_21_ALHI);
System_Sound30 := RISING_EDGE(DelugeFailedToRelease);  // Deluge Failed After 3 Pump B Attempts
System_Sound31 := RISING_EDGE(Pump_Active_1_Hour);     // Deluge Pump A 1-Hour Cutoff Reached

// Group C (System_Sound32..37, 40): PLC System Faults & Pump B Inhibited -> Triggers PLC_Fault_INT
System_Sound32 := RISING_EDGE(#BAD_RAM (%SA0001));
System_Sound33 := RISING_EDGE(#HRD_CPU (%SA0009));
System_Sound34 := RISING_EDGE(#HRD_FLT (%SA0010));
System_Sound35 := RISING_EDGE(#LOS_IOM (%SA0012));
System_Sound36 := RISING_EDGE(#LOS_RCK (%SA0011));
System_Sound37 := RISING_EDGE(#LOW_BAT (%SA0002));
System_Sound40 := RISING_EDGE(Pump_B_Inhibited_AL (%M00025));

// --- Rungs 39..45: Latch Sound Outputs on Any New Rising Edge ---
IF (ANY System_Sound01 .. System_Sound31) THEN
    LATCH Tag_DO_15_INT (%M00215) := TRUE;         // PCR Control Room Panel Buzzer
END_IF;

IF (ANY System_Sound01 .. System_Sound26) THEN
    LATCH SA_7404_001_002_INT (%M00202) := TRUE;   // Pump House Local Horn/Bell
END_IF;

IF (ANY System_Sound32 .. System_Sound37 OR System_Sound40) THEN
    LATCH PLC_Fault_INT (%M00216) := TRUE;         // PCR Panel Pulsed Fault Buzzer
END_IF;

GE Rungs: 4 L5X Rungs: 7 Called By: Output Calls: None

Drives the 4 fail-safe de-energize-to-trip shutdown relays: Fuel Gas ESD Solenoid (%Q0001), Main Pump Shutdown (%Q0008), Oil Booster Pump Shutdown (%Q0003), and Water Booster Pump Shutdown (%Q0004). Normal healthy state is ENERGIZED (1); trip state is DE-ENERGIZED (0). Supports HMI Maintenance Override (_MT) and the INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS keyswitch.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Shutdow) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Shutdow — Fail-Safe De-Energize-to-Trip Shutdown Outputs
// Source:  LAD/Shutdown.pdf (4 Rungs)
// Note:    All 4 outputs are FAIL-SAFE (1 = Energized / Healthy, 0 = De-Energized / Trip).
//          In GE VersaMax, Rung 1 uses normal COIL with NCCON contacts, while Rungs 2..4
//          use negated coils -( / )- (NCCOIL). Both produce identical fail-safe behavior!
// ============================================================================

// Rung 1: Fuel Gas ESD Valve Solenoid (%Q0001) — Energized (1) when healthy, 0 to close valve
EY_6401_001_002 (%Q00001) :=
    (NOT EY_6401_001_002_INT (%M00201) AND NOT EY_6401_001_002_MT (%M00281))
    OR INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00074);

// Rung 2: Main F&G Pump Shutdown Relay (%Q0008) — Negated Coil -( / )- (1 = Run, 0 = Shutdown)
PumpShutdown (%Q00008) :=
    NOT ((PumpShutdown_INT (%M00208) OR PumpShutdown_MT (%M00288))
         AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00074));

// Rung 3: Oil Booster Pumps P-2100 / P-2200 Shutdown Relay (%Q0003) — Negated Coil -( / )-
P2100_P2200 (%Q00003) :=
    NOT ((P2100_P2200_INT (%M00203) OR P2100_P2200_MT (%M00283))
         AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00074));

// Rung 4: Water Booster Pumps P-3600 / P-3700 Shutdown Relay (%Q0004) — Negated Coil -( / )-
P3600_P3700 (%Q00004) :=
    NOT ((P3600_P3700_INT (%M00204) OR P3600_P3700_MT (%M00284))
         AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00074));
1-to-1 Rung-by-Rung Pseudocode Translation (7 Rungs)
Rung / Source Structured Pseudocode & Ladder Logic
Rung 0
Shutdow rung 3 (GE) part 1/1 - %M00225, %M00161, %M00045 -> %Q00001; NCCON, NOCON, NOCON -> COIL (plain OTE, NOT inverted)
6401-EY-001/002 ESD fuel gas valve shutdown: the internal cause-and-effect bit EY_6401_001_002_INT (%M00225) is printed NC, so the output EY_6401_001_002 (%Q00001) drops when the trip is demanded and can only stay energised while the manual-trip bit EY_6401_001_002_MT (%M00161) is set. The parallel branch forces the output back to 1 when the all-outputs inhibit INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00045) is set. The printed coil is a plain OTE - this rung is not inverted.
EY_6401_001_002 := ((NOT EY_6401_001_002_INT AND EY_6401_001_002_MT) OR INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI);
[XIO(EY_6401_001_002_INT)XIC(EY_6401_001_002_MT),XIC(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI)]OTE(EY_6401_001_002);

Trip term for the fire & gas pump shutdown: the NO internal bit PumpShutdown_INT (%M00232, 1 = trip demanded) in series with the NC all-outputs inhibit INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00045). This is the printed condition BEFORE the negated coil is applied, so both printed contact polarities are kept exactly.
PumpShutdown_TRIP(%M00232) := PumpShutdown_INT AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI;
XIC(PumpShutdown_INT)XIO(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI)OTE(PumpShutdown_TRIP);

Do not simplify to a plain OTE. !! REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS: how the GE NCCOIL over a two-contact chain is split. The source equation is %Q00008 = NOT(%M00232 AND NOT %M00045) = NOT %M00232 OR %M00045, so with the inhibit (%M00045) set the output must stay at 1 (non-tripped), exactly as rung 3 of this routine forces %Q00001 to 1 with the same inhibit. The two-rung form used here (trip term, then XIO(trip term)OTE(Q00008)) is algebraically identical and keeps the printed NC inhibit as XIO. The alternative single-rung forms are XIO(PumpShutdown_INT)XIO(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI)OTE(PumpShutdown) - NOT equivalent, it de-energises and TRIPS %Q00008 when the inhibit is active - and [XIO(PumpShutdown_INT),XIC(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI)]OTE(PumpShutdown), which is equivalent but inverts the printed inhibit polarity. Flagged for plant confirmation of the inhibit convention.
PumpShutdown := NOT PumpShutdown_TRIP(%M00232);
XIO(PumpShutdown_TRIP)OTE(PumpShutdown);

P2100_P2200_TRIP(%M00227) := P2100_P2200_INT AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI;
XIC(P2100_P2200_INT)XIO(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI)OTE(P2100_P2200_TRIP);

Do not simplify to a plain OTE. !! REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS: same negated-coil split as rung 4; %Q00003 = NOT(%M00227 AND NOT %M00045) = NOT %M00227 OR %M00045. The literal XIO(P2100_P2200_INT)XIO(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI)OTE(P2100_P2200) form is NOT equivalent - it trips %Q00003 whenever the all-outputs inhibit is active, contradicting rung 3 - while [XIO(P2100_P2200_INT),XIC(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI)]OTE(P2100_P2200) is equivalent but inverts the printed inhibit polarity.

GE Rungs: 7 L5X Rungs: 17 Called By: Output Calls: None

Drives the Deluge Skid outputs (Pump A Start/Stop %Q0005, Pump B Start %Q0007, Pump B Stop %Q0006) gated by both Inhibit keyswitches (INHIBIT_FOAM_REL and INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS). Also generates a 2-second continuity test pulse every 60 seconds (via #T_MIN and 28s timers T00013/T00014) to verify coil wiring continuity on %Q0005 and %Q0007, latching an Open-Circuit fault (PUMP_A_OC / PUMP_B_START_OC) if feedback fails for 70 seconds.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Protect) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Protect — Deluge Pump Relays & Coil Continuity Supervision
// Source:  LAD/Protect.pdf (7 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// --- Rungs 1..3: Deluge Skid Physical Relay Outputs ---
PUMP_A (%Q00005) :=
    (PUMP_A_INT (%M00205) OR PUMP_A_MT (%M00285))
    AND NOT INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI    (%M00073)
    AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00074);

PUMP_B_START (%Q00007) :=
    (PUMP_B_START_INT (%M00207) OR PUMP_B_START_MT (%M00287))
    AND NOT INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI    (%M00073)
    AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00074);

PUMP_B_STOP (%Q00006) :=
    PUMP_B_STOP_INT (%M00206) OR PUMP_B_STOP_MT (%M00286);

// --- Rungs 4..5: Pump A Start Circuit Continuity Supervision (70s Watchdog) ---
// #T_MIN (%S00006) is HIGH for 30s and LOW for 30s every minute.
// Pump_Timer11 (PV = 28.0s) turns ON T00013 for the last 2.0s of every 30s #T_MIN HIGH half-cycle.
ONDTR(Pump_Timer11, Enable := T00002 AND #T_MIN, Reset := NOT #T_MIN, PV := 28.0s) -> T00013;
Pump_A_PulsOut_INT (%M00233) := (T00013 AND T00002) OR PUMP_A (%Q00005);

// If feedback Pump_A_PulsIn_ALI (%M00057) does not pulse at least once every 70.0s, flag Open Circuit:
ONDTR(Pump_Timer12,
      Enable := T00002 AND ((NOT Pump_A_PulsIn_ALI AND NOT PUMP_A_INT) OR (PUMP_A_INT AND Pump_A_PulsIn_ALI)),
      Reset  := Pump_A_PulsIn_ALI OR PUMP_A_INT,
      PV     := 70.0s) -> PUMP_A_OC (%M00293);

// --- Rungs 6..7: Pump B Start Circuit Continuity Supervision (70s Watchdog) ---
ONDTR(Pump_Timer10, Enable := T00002 AND #T_MIN, Reset := NOT #T_MIN, PV := 28.0s) -> T00014;
Pump_B_Start_PulsOut_INT (%M00234) := (T00014 AND T00002) OR PUMP_B_START (%Q00007);

ONDTR(Pump_Timer13,
      Enable := T00002 AND ((NOT Pump_B_Start_PulsIn_ALI AND NOT PUMP_B_START_INT) OR (PUMP_B_START_INT AND Pump_B_Start_PulsIn_ALI)),
      Reset  := Pump_B_Start_PulsIn_ALI,
      PV     := 70.0s) -> PUMP_B_START_OC (%M00295);

Deluge pump A start/stop internal cause-and-effect bit PUMP_A_INT (%M00229) drives the field output PUMP_A (%Q00005) through the foam-release inhibit INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI (%M00044) and the all-outputs inhibit INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00045); both inhibits are printed NC so they are XIO. Page banner for this part of the block: 'Fire Protection Outputs set in this block.'
PUMP_A := PUMP_A_INT AND NOT INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI;
XIC(PUMP_A_INT)XIO(INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI)XIO(INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI)OTE(PUMP_A);

⚙ Loc_Al LAD/Loc_AI.pdf ↗

GE Rungs: 3 L5X Rungs: 3 Called By: Output Calls: None

Drives the Pump House Alarm Horn/Bell (%Q0002), PCR Panel Steady Alarm Buzzer (%Q0015), and PCR Panel 1Hz Pulsed PLC Fault Sounder (%Q0016). Note: The steady panel alarm (Tag_DO_15) suppresses the pulsed fault sounder (PLC_Fault) so both do not clash.

Structured Algorithmic Pseudocode (Loc_Al) 
// ============================================================================
// ROUTINE: Loc_Al — Local & Control Room Audible Alarm Outputs
// Source:  LAD/Loc_AI.pdf (3 Rungs)
// ============================================================================

// Rung 1: Pump House Local Alarm Horn/Bell (%Q0002)
SA_7404_001_002 (%Q00002) :=
    (SA_7404_001_002_INT (%M00202) OR SA_7404_001_002_MT (%M00282))
    AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00074);

// Rung 2: PCR Control Panel Steady Alarm Buzzer (%Q0015)
Tag_DO_15 (%Q00015) :=
    (Tag_DO_15_INT (%M00215) OR Tag_DO_15_MT (%M00295))
    AND NOT INHIBIT_ALL_OUTPUTS_ALI (%M00074);

// Rung 3: PCR Control Panel Pulsed PLC Fault Buzzer (%Q0016)
// Pulsed at 1 Hz using #T_SEC (%S00005); suppressed when steady alarm buzzer Tag_DO_15 is active.
PLC_Fault (%Q00016) :=
    ((PLC_Fault_INT (%M00216) AND NOT Tag_DO_15 (%Q00015)) OR PLC_Fault_MT (%M00296))
    AND #T_SEC (%S00005);
1-to-1 Rung-by-Rung Pseudocode Translation (3 Rungs)
Rung / Source Structured Pseudocode & Ladder Logic
Rung 0
Loc_Al rung 2 (GE) - NOCON SA_7404_001_002_INT %M00226 series NCCON INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI %M00044 -> COIL SA_7404_001_002 %Q00002
Series chain: NO contact SA_7404_001_002_INT (%M00226, '7404-SA-001/002 Local alarm pump house - Internal C_E use') followed by NC contact INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI (%M00044, 'Foam release inhibit - Alarm inhibit'), driving the unlatched output coil SA_7404_001_002 (%Q00002, '7404-SA-001/002 Local alarm pump house'). The local alarm output follows the internal bit unless the foam release / alarm inhibit is active, in which case it is forced off.
SA_7404_001_002 := SA_7404_001_002_INT AND NOT INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI;
XIC(SA_7404_001_002_INT)XIO(INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI)OTE(SA_7404_001_002);
Rung 1
Loc_Al rung 3 (GE) - NOCON Tag_DO_15_INT %M00239 series NCCON INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI %M00044 -> COIL Tag_DO_15 %Q00015
Series chain: NO contact Tag_DO_15_INT (%M00239, 'Panel alarm - Internal C_E use') followed by the same NC contact INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI (%M00044), driving the output coil Tag_DO_15 (%Q00015, 'Panel alarm'). The panel alarm output is therefore also suppressed while the foam release / alarm inhibit is active.
Tag_DO_15 := Tag_DO_15_INT AND NOT INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI;
XIC(Tag_DO_15_INT)XIO(INHIBIT_FOAM_REL_ALI)OTE(Tag_DO_15);
Rung 2
Loc_Al rung 4 (GE) - NOCON PLC_Fault_INT %M00240 series NCCON Tag_DO_15 %Q00015 -> COIL PLC_Fault %Q00016
Series chain: NO contact PLC_Fault_INT (%M00240, 'Set when PLC fault exists - Internal C_E use') followed by the NC contact Tag_DO_15 (%Q00015), driving the output coil PLC_Fault (%Q00016, 'SpareDO-16'). Note the second contact has no inhibit in this rung: it is a NC contact on the Tag_DO_15 output bit itself, so the PLC fault output is blocked while the local panel alarm is energised.
PLC_Fault := PLC_Fault_INT AND NOT Tag_DO_15;
XIC(PLC_Fault_INT)XIO(Tag_DO_15)OTE(PLC_Fault);
